_meta.purpose: Focused slice for building and testing the reorderable ranking-criteria panel. Attach THIS file to a design prompt instead of the full bundle when you only need the ranking feature.
_meta.howToUse: Render the criteria as a drag-to-reorder list. On every reorder, recompute each application's score with the weight formula and re-sort. Nothing is pre-sorted for you except the scenarios below, which exist so you can verify your maths.

rankingModel.formula: weight(i) = (N - i + 1) / (N * (N + 1) / 2), where i is the 1-indexed position of the criterion and N is how many criteria the posting uses.
rankingModel.score: aiRankScore = round( sum over criteria of weight(position) * application.criterionScores[criterionId] ). Scores are 0-100.
rankingModel.scoresAreStoredForEveryCriterion: Each application carries a score and a note for ALL criteria in the catalog, not only the ones the posting currently uses. That means the recruiter can both REORDER the chosen criteria and SWAP one out for another, and the UI recomputes the whole candidate list client-side with no server round trip.
rankingModel.postingUsesThreeToFive: A posting's rankingCriteria array holds between 3 and 5 criterion ids, in priority order. Position 1 is the highest priority.
rankingModel.explainabilityRule: Show the note for the TWO highest-weighted criteria. If the candidate's score on that criterion is >= 70 present it as a reason; if < 55 present it as a concern; between 55 and 69 present it neutrally. Reasons and concerns must change when the recruiter reorders the criteria — they are derived, never stored as prose.
rankingModel.eligibilityRule: Candidates with profileCompleteness < 70 are not scored at all (aiRankScore is null) and appear in a separate 'Not yet rankable' group.
rankingModel.humanInTheLoop: Ranking orders a list. It never rejects, filters out, or hides a candidate, and it never makes a hiring decision.

criteriaCatalog.label: Years of experience
criteriaCatalog.description: Total classroom years, weighted toward years in the posting's subject.

criteriaCatalog.label: Curriculum experience
criteriaCatalog.description: Overlap between the curricula the candidate has taught and those the posting requires (IB, Cambridge, AP).

criteriaCatalog.label: Subject specialisation
criteriaCatalog.description: How closely the candidate's primary specialism matches the posted subject.

criteriaCatalog.label: Advanced degree
criteriaCatalog.description: Highest qualification held — doctorate, master's, or bachelor's.

criteriaCatalog.label: Availability
criteriaCatalog.description: Whether the candidate is free by the posting's start date, and how much margin there is.

criteriaCatalog.label: Verified supervisor references
criteriaCatalog.description: Number of verified references from direct supervisors or heads of school. Peer references do not count.

criteriaCatalog.label: Regional experience
criteriaCatalog.description: Prior international placement, weighted toward the school's own region.

criteriaCatalog.label: Leadership experience
criteriaCatalog.description: Years in a coordination, head-of-department or senior-leadership role.

criteriaCatalog.label: Coaching & activities
criteriaCatalog.description: Willingness and ability to lead an after-school activity or sport.

criteriaCatalog.label: Local hire
criteriaCatalog.description: Already holds the right to work in the school's country — no relocation package or work permit needed.
